group: No ID, simple absolute JSON Pointer

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/properties/name' (e.g., {"type":"string"})
cases.description: The schema has no ID, the reference starts with '/' so it is treated as an absolute JSON Pointer. The method should return the node found at that pointer.

group: Schema ID present and reference starts with the ID

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/properties/age' (e.g., {"type":"integer"})
cases.description: The schema's getId() returns 'http://example.com/schema'. Because the reference starts with this ID, the ID part is stripped, leaving '#/properties/age'. The leading '#/' is then removed, yielding '/properties/age', which is used to locate the node.

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/definitions/person' (e.g., {"type":"object", ...})
cases.description: No schema ID is involved. The reference begins with '#/', so the method removes the leading '#', leaving '/definitions/person', and returns the node at that pointer.

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/properties/first name' (decoded space) (e.g., {"type":"string"})
cases.description: The pointer contains percent‑encoded characters. After confirming it starts with '/', the method URL‑decodes it to '/properties/first name' before locating the node.

cases.expected: JsonNode returned by handleNullNode(ref, schema) (fallback node)
cases.description: The pointer points to a location that does not exist in the schema. After node.at() returns a missing node, the method invokes handleNullNode and returns its result.

group: Reference does not start with '/' or '#/' – returns root schema node

cases.description: The reference neither starts with the schema ID, '#/', nor '/' so none of the conditional blocks modify jsonPointer. The method should simply return the root schema node.

group: ID present, reference starts with ID but without fragment '#'

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/properties/name' (e.g., {"type":"string"})
cases.description: The schema's getId() returns 'http://example.com/schema'. The reference starts with this ID but does not contain a fragment. The method strips the ID, leaving '/properties/name', decodes it (no change), and returns the node found at that JSON Pointer.

group: ID present, reference starts with ID but concatenated without leading '/' after ID

cases.description: The reference starts with the schema ID but the remaining part does not begin with '/' or '#/'. After stripping the ID the pointer becomes 'properties/name', which does not satisfy the '/' check, so the method returns the root schema node.

group: Reference equals the schema ID exactly

cases.description: When the reference is exactly the same as the schema ID, stripping the ID leaves an empty string. Because the resulting pointer does not start with '/' or '#/', the method returns the root schema node.
An empty reference does not trigger any of the conditional branches, so the method returns the root schema node unchanged.
A solitary '#' is not followed by '/', therefore after the '#/' check the pointer remains '#'. It does not start with '/', so the method returns the root schema node.

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the first element of the 'items' array (e.g., {"type":"string"})
cases.description: The reference points to an array element using a numeric index. After decoding, node.at('/items/0') returns the node at that position.

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/properties/address/street' (e.g., {"type":"string"})
cases.description: The pointer contains an encoded '/' (%2F). The method decodes it to '/properties/address/street' before invoking node.at, thus locating the correct node.

cases.expected: JsonNode representing the schema node located at '/definitions/emptyId' (e.g., {"type":"object"})
cases.description: When schema.getId() returns an empty string, the condition `schema.getId() != null && ref.startsWith(schema.getId())` is true (empty string is a prefix of any string). The method strips the empty ID, leaving the original pointer unchanged, then proceeds normally.
Calling getRefSchemaNode with a null reference should cause a NullPointerException when the method attempts to evaluate ref.startsWith(...).
If findSchemaResourceRoot() returns null, the subsequent call to schema.getSchemaNode() dereferences a null object, resulting in a NullPointerException.
When the schema returned by findSchemaResourceRoot() has a null schema node (getSchemaNode() returns null), the method attempts to call node.at(...), which throws a NullPointerException.
